data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and reviewing weak units (1 & 2) to ensure readiness for the exam.
data.summary: This 16-week plan prioritizes the student's weak units (1 and 2) in the first half, integrating live classes for Units 1 and 2. The middle weeks cover Units 3-7, while the final weeks focus on Units 8-9 and mixed review. Each week includes concrete tasks and stays within the 4-hour limit.

tasks: Do 10 practice problems on molar mass calculations and stoichiometry basics.
Analyze 5 mass spectra to determine isotopic composition and average atomic mass.
Calculate percent composition for 5 pure substances.
Solve 3 mixture composition problems using density and mass percent.
Write electron configurations for 10 elements, including transition metals.
Interpret 5 photoelectron spectra to identify elements based on binding energy.
Create a chart of periodic trends for ionization energy, atomic radius, and electronegativity.
Predict ionic charges for 10 elements based on valence electrons.
Attend live class on Unit 1.
Do 5 free-response questions on atomic structure and properties.

weeks.focus: Types of chemical bonds and potential energy
tasks: Classify 10 compounds as ionic, covalent, or metallic.
Draw potential energy diagrams for 3 bond formation processes.

weeks.focus: Structure of ionic solids and metals
tasks: Analyze crystal lattice structures for 3 ionic compounds.
Explain properties of 3 metals based on their structure.
Draw Lewis structures for 8 molecules, including resonance forms.
Calculate formal charges for 5 molecules with multiple resonance structures.
Predict molecular geometry for 10 molecules using VSEPR theory.
Determine hybridization for 5 central atoms in various molecules.

weeks.focus: Intermolecular forces and properties of solids
tasks: Identify dominant intermolecular forces for 8 substances.
Compare boiling points of 5 liquids based on intermolecular forces.

weeks.focus: Ideal gas law and kinetic molecular theory
tasks: Solve 5 ideal gas law problems involving pressure, volume, and temperature.
Explain gas behavior using kinetic molecular theory for 3 scenarios.
Balance 10 chemical equations and write net ionic equations for 5 reactions.
Perform stoichiometric calculations for 3 limiting reactant problems.
Calculate reaction rates from concentration-time data for 3 reactions.
Determine rate laws and rate constants for 2 reactions using experimental data.
Calculate heat transfer for 5 endothermic and exothermic processes.
Use calorimetry data to determine enthalpy changes for 3 reactions.
Write equilibrium expressions for 5 reversible reactions.
Calculate equilibrium constants and reaction quotients for 3 systems.
Complete a 45-minute timed practice set covering Units 1-2.
Review 10 free-response questions from Units 3-9 and mark them against the scoring guide.
